organic farming is not a sustainable production system in coffee.

In summary, our research is concerned with

the following topics: • The effect of shade on the incidence and severity of coffee leaf rust (Hemileia vastatrix) in the highlands of Costa Rica • The effect of coffee leaf rust on the yield and quality of coffee in the highlands • The effect of the shade tree species on the incidence and intensity of coffee leaf rust in the highlands and lowlands of Costa Rica
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
organic coffee, as presently practised, is neither economically nor ecologically sustainable.
the organic concept is a good idea but the implementation in its present form is not.
organic coffee production is not sustainable in the strict sense, but that sustainable coffee production is sustainable in the strictest sense.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the organic concept of coffee production, as presently applied, is not sustainable, but that the principles of organic production can be adopted to make coffee production more sustainable, if not truly organic.

we need to be more critical of the concept of organic coffee production, while we should be less sceptical about the potential for sustainable production of high-quality coffees by applying best practices.
organic coffee production in its strict sense is not sustainable and does not serve the interest of the producer and the consumer as much as its proponents would have us believe.
The main takeaway from our work is that

organic coffee is not a panacea for the problems facing the coffee sector in developing countries, but it can be an effective tool for the promotion of sustainable coffee production if the preconditions are adapted to the local situation and the benefits are shared equitably between the various stakeholders.
the organic coffee industry should focus on the production of high-quality coffees, which can be achieved through sustainable production methods.
organic coffee production is not necessarily a more sustainable option compared to conventional coffee farming.
